title: Sectionwise invariance of Hom complexes into K-injectives
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, $s:I^{\prime\bullet}\to I^\bullet$ a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] between K-injective complexes [def-pur-kinjective-complex], and $t:L^{\prime\bullet}\to L^\bullet$ a quasi-isomorphism of cochain complexes of $R$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. For every site object $U$, the section map $\Gamma(U,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L,I^{\prime})\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L^{\prime},I))$ induced by precomposition with $t$ and postcomposition with $s$ is a quasi-isomorphism of abelian-group complexes. Here the Hom complexes are those of [def-pur-hom-complex].

proof.text: For a fixed object U and degree n, identify the degree-n cohomology of sections with degree-zero cohomology for the first argument shifted by -n. The product projections and signed differential in def-pur-hom-complex identify cocycles with localized chain maps and boundaries with null-homotopies. These identifications commute with pre- and postcomposition. Apply lem-pur-rhom-into-kinjective-local to both shifted first arguments and K-injective targets.

Restriction to the localized module site is exact and preserves K-injectives, by its adjunction with exact extension by zero. Thus restricted s and shifted t remain quasi-isomorphisms. Their derived-localization images are isomorphisms. On the Hom groups the induced map is precomposition and postcomposition with these isomorphisms, and the reverse compositions with their inverses give its inverse. Consequently every homology map on sections is bijective and hence an isomorphism in abelian groups.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 0A95, with the degreewise and exact-sheafification argument spelled out
